method: Fat and sugar are balanced by weight against the finished mix, which is treated as cream, milk and sugar only. Sugar grams are the batch weight times the sugar target over 100, and the rest of the batch is dairy. The cream weight c is the one that makes the fat add up: c times the cream fat percentage plus the remaining dairy times the milk fat percentage must equal the batch times the butterfat target, so c = (batch x fat - milkFat x dairy) / (creamFat - milkFat) with every percentage taken as a fraction. Milk is the rest of the dairy, and the fat each ingredient carries is reported so the two contributions can be checked against the target. Defaults are a 1,000 g base at 12 percent butterfat and 16 percent sugar from 36 percent cream and 3.5 percent whole milk; in the United States the name ice cream requires at least 10 percent milk fat, and premium recipes commonly sit at 12 to 16. Batch weights are accepted from 100 to 20,000 g, the butterfat target from 1 to 30 percent, sugar from 5 to 30 percent, cream fat from 20 to 50 percent and milk fat from 0 to 15 percent, and decimal commas are accepted. The target must lie strictly between the milk fat and the cream fat, cream fat must exceed milk fat, and a combination whose cream alone would outweigh the dairy - a high fat target with a lot of sugar - is refused rather than returning a negative milk weight. Weights are rounded to 0.1 g and percentages to 0.1, so the rounded parts can miss the batch by a tenth. Milk solids other than fat, egg yolk, stabilisers, flavourings and water lost to cooking are not modelled, and nothing is claimed about freezing point, overrun, texture or food safety. The page runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Ice cream: in the United States the name ice cream requires at least 10 percent milk fat and at least 180 g of solids per litre.
Wikipedia, Cream: cream is graded by butterfat content, with cream sold without further specification at 35 percent milk fat or more and manufacturing cream from 40 percent.
Wikipedia, Milk: whole milk is about 3.5 percent fat by weight, with semi-skimmed and skimmed grades lower.
